input.brief: Bellis Australia: industrial mechanical insulation distributor, metal fabricator and installer serving LNG, power, mining, marine and defence plants

direction.name: The printed annual
direction.idea: Lay the page out like a well-designed printed report or magazine feature: a masthead image, a tight oversized title, text held to a strict column line, and colour used in solid blocks the way a two-colour print job would. It gives weight and authority to subjects that are really about content: findings, a manifesto, a programme, a serious product. The reader should feel that someone edited this.
direction.composition: A fixed vertical axis at about 42% of the viewport width organises everything: headings begin on it, body columns hang from it, and the 0–42% zone holds small side notes, figures or stays empty. Masthead: a wide image band (photographic mosaic or a single crop) across the top 45% of the first screen; below it the title at 7–9vw starting on the axis, with a two-sentence standfirst at 20–24px. Sections alternate between text pages (title on the axis, body in one or two columns of 34–40ch to its right) and full-bleed colour pages carrying one large figure, quotation or image mosaic. Mosaics are gutterless: photographs and flat colour tiles butted together in a 4- or 6-cell grid. Page numbers, running heads and other print furniture are left out.
direction.typography: A tight heavy grotesk or a sharp serif for titles; an excellent text face for reading at 18–20px with leading near 1.5. Headings in sentence case, tracked tight.
direction.colour: Paper, ink and two or three solid block colours. A colour page is a whole section in one flat colour.
direction.imagery: Photographs used as blocks in mosaics alongside flat colour tiles; mixed subjects are fine if cropped tight and converted to one treatment.
direction.photoTreatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.
direction.richness: The column line, the mosaics and whole pages of colour give structure and variety without ornaments.
direction.pitfalls: The axis must be exact and reused everywhere or it reads as random indentation. Keep paragraphs to a real reading measure. On a phone the axis collapses to the left margin and side notes move inline above their paragraph.

hero.name: Narrow talk, wide headline
hero.blueprint: An asymmetric sheet on one flat paper-grey ground, divided at 34% of the width by alignment only. Left column (columns 1-4, 32px margin): the wordmark top-left; then, starting at 30% of the height, one supporting sentence at 22px with leading 1.35, max 24ch; under it the single action, a solid ink rectangle with square corners. The column's lower third is empty. Right column (columns 5-12): four text links at 15px on its top edge, the first aligned exactly to the 34% line. Beneath them the headline in a very heavy grotesk at clamp(88px, 9.8vw, 150px), two lines, line-height 0.82, tracking -0.04em, flush left on the 34% line and filling the column width. A square-cornered photograph the full width of the right column starts at 68% of the viewport height and is cropped by the bottom edge. A solid accent block 260px wide, carrying one real figure at 40px and one line of text, overlaps the photograph's top-left corner by half its own height using a negative top margin.
hero.mobile: One column on 20px margins. The wordmark and a menu word share the top row. The headline comes first at 15vw on two lines, heavy, line-height 0.85. The supporting sentence follows at 18px, then the action at full width. The photograph runs full bleed below at 4:3, with the accent block overlapping its top-left corner at 60% of the screen width.
hero.headline: A 2-4 word statement in the heaviest weight, at most 20 characters, one or two words per line.

type.note: The plain Times-style roman of a typed document, slightly tightened and never larger than a few vw. Suits vehicles and tools presented dryly, artists' pages, investment memos and anything meant to look undesigned on purpose.

palette.name: Plum-black and pink
palette.note: Near-black and plum at the top and bottom bracket a white middle with navy-black text. Hot pink is reserved for primary buttons, bars in charts and map markers; it never fills a section.

photos.title: Objects
photos.note: single objects seen close: instruments, tools, cameras, books
photos.treatment: Give all photographs in a mosaic one treatment: greyscale via `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)`, or all full colour. Do not mix.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Comparison set as text
sections.blueprint: A comparison table with no lines and no tick marks. A CSS grid: capability names in columns 1–5 of 12 at 22–24px medium, then three answer columns of equal width (plans, methods, or this against the usual way). Every cell answers in words at 17px: 'Yes, unlimited', 'Up to five', 'Not yet', never a symbol. Seven to ten rows, each 64–72px tall, with every other row on a ground one tone darker so the eye tracks across; rows touch. The column that matters is one filled block in the accent or ink colour running the full height of the table behind its cells and rising 24px above the first row, with its text reversed. Column names sit in the top row at 17px bold. The heading, two to four words at 40–48px, hangs top-left above column 1 with 48px beneath.
sections.mobile: The table turns on its side: one block per capability. The name at 20px bold, then three lines beneath, each giving a column name and its answer at 16px; the featured column's line is set on the filled colour at full width. Blocks alternate the two ground tones.

sections.name: Band of unequal panels
sections.blueprint: A modest heading, then one wide band of pictures. The heading, two to four words at 36–44px, starts at column 3, left of centre, with 64px beneath it. The band spans the full viewport width edge to edge and is 68svh tall: four photographs standing side by side with no gaps and deliberately unequal widths, a flex row with flex-grow values of 5, 2, 3 and 2. Each panel is cropped with object-fit: cover to a tall slice, so the band reads as one folded view. The first panel carries a two-line title at 28px in paper colour at its top-left, 24px in, over a neutral scrim that covers only that corner. Hovering a panel raises its flex-grow to 6 over 500ms while the others give way; without hover the widths simply stay. One caption line at 16px sits under the band at the left margin.
sections.mobile: The heading sits on the margin at 28px. The band becomes a two-by-two block with no gaps, 84svh tall in total: the first row split 64/36 and the second 36/64, so the slices stay unequal. The title stays on the first panel. No hover behaviour.

sections.name: Lines that step across
sections.blueprint: The sequence is written, not counted. Four lines of display type, one stage per line, each a complete short clause that begins with its order word: 'First you send it.' 'Then we take it apart.' 'You choose one.' 'It ships on Friday.' Set at clamp(36px, 4.6vw, 76px), leading 1.0, one line each. The first line starts on column 1 and each following line starts two columns further right (grid-column-start 1, 3, 5, 7), so the block descends as a staircase and the eye follows the diagonal. Under each line, on that line's own left edge and 12px below, a sentence of up to 34ch at 17px in the soft ink. 56px between stages. The last line may take the accent colour as the single emphasis. The first line serves as the heading; there is no title above. Leave the columns to the left of the final stage empty.
sections.mobile: Lines drop to 8.4vw and may wrap onto a second line. The staircase becomes a smaller indent of 6vw per stage, so the fourth line starts 18vw in. Each sentence sits under its line at 16px on the same indent. 40px between stages.

sections.name: Plain names in columns
sections.blueprint: A typographic list with no logos. The heading, two or three words at 28–32px, sits in columns 1–3 and stays top-aligned with the first row of names. Columns 5–12 hold the names in three or four text columns (`columns: 4; column-gap: 32px`), each name on its own line at 20–22px with leading 1.5, sentence case, in the full ink. Where names fall into kinds (clients, press, partners), each kind starts a new column and its first line names the kind in the softer ink at the same size, so no small labels are needed. Columns are of unequal length and are not balanced; ragged bottoms are intended. Twelve to thirty names work best. There are no boxes, bullets or separators: the column edges and the shared baseline do the organising. Leave 120px above and below.
sections.mobile: The heading leads at 26px. Names follow in two columns at 17px with a 20px gap; each kind begins after a 32px break with its name in the softer ink on the first line. Long names wrap inside their column rather than shrinking.

sections.name: Column aligned on the decimal
sections.blueprint: A tall column of figures set like a ledger. Left, columns 1–5: the heading as a statement of up to five words on two lines at clamp(32px, 3.2vw, 52px), its first line in the soft ink and its second in full ink, placed at mid-height. Right, columns 7–12: four to six figures stacked, each at clamp(64px, 7vw, 112px), leading 1.0, in tabular lining numerals. They align on the decimal point: each row is a three-part grid in which the whole-number part is right-aligned in the first track, the point and decimals are left-aligned in the second, and a caption of one or two lines at 16px sits in the third, on the figure's baseline. Whole numbers simply leave the second track empty. Rows are separated by 20px of space only. Units are written in the captions, not attached to the figures, so the numerals form one clean vertical shape.
sections.mobile: The heading comes first at 28px. Figures drop to 15vw and keep the decimal alignment, with the split at 52% of the width. Each caption moves under its figure at 15px, starting from the left margin. 28px between rows.

sections.name: Cards that fold into spines
sections.blueprint: For a journal, a run of notes or a list of chapters without pictures. A wrapper about 400svh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh. The heading, two to four words at clamp(48px, 4.2vw, 64px), sits top-left on the 32px margin, 120px from the top. Under it a band 360px tall spans the content width and holds a horizontal deck of text cards, each about 620px wide, in three neighbouring flat tones of one hue taken in turn. On a card, with 32px padding: its title at 30px on up to two lines, leading 1.1; an excerpt of two lines at 16px; and along the bottom edge the date on the left and a text link to read it on the right, both at 16px. As the page scrolls, each step slides the next card in from the right edge and squeezes the earlier ones into slivers 120px wide stacked edge to edge at the left, like book spines, where only the first letters of their titles show, clipped by the sliver. Clicking a sliver brings its card back. 48px under the band, the number of entries and a link to the full list sit at 17px on the left margin, so the stage does not end on an empty floor.
sections.mobile: No pin and no slivers. The cards stack at full width with 12px gaps, each in its tone, the title at 24px, the excerpt at 16px, the date and link at the foot. The heading sits above them at 10vw.

sections.name: Sentence, portrait, two links
sections.blueprint: One closing row of three elements hanging from the same top line, with open ground between them, on a 12-column grid. Columns 1–5: a sentence of 12–18 words at clamp(26px, 3vw, 44px), four lines, leading 1.1, saying what kind of enquiries are welcome; it is set as a paragraph and there is no separate heading. Columns 8–9: one small square portrait or photograph of the place, 150–170px, with square corners. Columns 10–12: a short question at 18px in medium weight, then 20px below it two underlined links stacked at 18px (the email address and one booking or social link), and beneath them a line at 14px in the soft ink with the city and the usual reply time. Columns 6–7 stay empty. The row has 160px of space above and 120px below. No form. On a dark ground the photograph is the only bright thing in the row.
sections.mobile: The sentence comes first at 7.4vw. Below it the portrait at 96px square sits at the left margin with the question and the two links to its right, top-aligned, in the remaining width. The city and reply-time line spans the full width beneath.

sections.name: Three photographs, then a field
sections.blueprint: Two parts with no gap between them. First, a strip of three photographs butted edge to edge across the full viewport, each one third wide and 40svh tall, `object-fit: cover`, no gutters and no captions; give all three the same treatment. Directly beneath, a band in one flat palette colour, about 44svh tall. In the band, columns 1–7: the closing statement at 26–30px over three lines in the band's assigned ink, with exactly one phrase underlined by a 4px bar (`text-decoration-thickness: 4px; text-underline-offset: 6px`), and that phrase is the link; two lines at 16px follow 32px lower. In the lower-right corner, columns 11–12, a small portrait photograph (4:5, about 150px wide) sits 40px from the band's edges: the person who will answer. There is no button; the underlined phrase is the action.
sections.mobile: The strip becomes one full-width photograph at 4:3 with the other two side by side beneath it at half width each, still gutterless. The band follows: statement at 22px, the two small lines, and the portrait at 96px wide in the bottom-right corner.

sections.name: Name first, places under it
sections.blueprint: The wordmark opens the footer instead of closing it. On a full-bleed field in the page's inverse or final chapter colour, the name spans the full content width as the first thing, its cap line pushed 8% above the footer's top edge so the tops of the letters are sliced off by the section (`overflow: hidden` and a negative top margin in `em`). 72px beneath, a two-part row: columns 1–5 list the places or ways to reach the studio (cities, or email and telephone), one per line at 32–36px in the accent ink, each a link; columns 7–12 hold three columns of small links at 15px, top-aligned with the first place. A final row 96px lower carries the legal line at the left and a back-to-top text link at the right, both 13px. The field is about 90svh tall, and nothing sits between the wordmark and the row but space.
sections.mobile: The sliced wordmark stays at the top, fitted to the width. Places follow as a list at 26px, then the link columns two across at 15px. Legal line and back-to-top link share the last row at 12px, at opposite margins.

references.name: Artem Taradash
references.idea: A designer's CV compressed into one newspaper-like band at the top, after which oversized product renders and project artefacts speak at full scale.
references.hero: White page with 20px margins. Top-left are three small black rectangular tags with white text (name and two links). Below them a three-line statement at about 3vw in regular-weight grotesk fills the first third, left-aligned. To its right, starting at the very top edge, run two narrow columns of 12px text, then a third column listing clients one per line, and in the far top-right a circular portrait about 200px wide with a white hand-lettered word across the face. This text band ends by a quarter of the height. Below it a huge cut-out vehicle render bleeds off the bottom, with a project card at right.
references.type: One family, Diatype, in regular weight throughout. Three sizes: about 43px for statements and project titles, 12.4px for all running text, about 11px for tags. Tight leading, sentence case, no bold and no capitals; hierarchy comes from size alone.
references.colour: #ffffff #111111 #f7f9fb #1c4fd8 #f0a23a — Strictly black on white for the frame. All colour arrives with project material: an orange-to-blue gradient, a cobalt zigzag pattern, warm photography.
references.imagery: Product renders cut out on white and shown very large, interface screenshots with a small corner radius, a full-width studio photo with a circular logo overlaid, and textile-pattern fields running margin to margin. Scale varies sharply between projects.
references.layout: A loose six-column grid with 20px margins; small text blocks hang from column lines beside very large images. Each project is arranged differently, and there are no dividers or section backgrounds, only white space and jumps in scale. The tag nav stays fixed top-left.

sections.description: Each project pairs one oversized visual with a small caption cluster. In the first, a cut-out product render fills the left 60% and bleeds off the edge. The right third stacks a landscape screenshot with slightly rounded corners, then a row holding a tiny label and two-line title at about 3vw on the left and a five-line 12px description on the right.

A row of three: a round black watch-face mock-up about a quarter of the width, a wide rectangle filled with a horizontal blue, violet, orange, blue gradient with a tiny tick scale beneath it, and a narrow text column at far right with label, three-line title and two short paragraphs. Circle, rectangle and text share a top line.

A cobalt-and-white zigzag textile pattern runs margin to margin for more than a full viewport height with only a two-line caption beneath it at left. Before it, a black-backed mosaic of pattern samples and report-cover mock-ups sits beside two narrow text columns. The pattern is given a section to itself with no mock-up frame.

Closing row on white: a tiny label, then a four-line sentence at about 3vw in the left third; a small square portrait at the two-thirds mark; to its right a short question with two underlined links below. All three hang from the same top line with empty space between them.

steal: Put bio, client list and portrait in one compact multi-column band at the top so the first scroll is already work.
Use solid black rectangular tags with white text as the only navigation chrome.
Let one project artefact (a pattern, a gradient) run full width for a whole screen with a two-line caption instead of framing it in a mock-up.

references.name: Ai in Design Report 2026
references.idea: A research report laid out like a colour-blocked print annual: a thermal-blurred video collage on top, an oversized tight grotesk title, and flat orange, lilac, sage and black blocks carrying stats, quotes and chapters.
references.hero: The top 53% is a full-width video band: blurred, heat-map-like abstract footage in orange, lilac and sage, overlaid with four or five hard-edged rectangles of the same footage in grey or green, two tagged with tiny mono labels in white boxes. The header sits flush on top: a black logo block at far left, an orange link tab running to 40% of the width, two plain links at right. Below the band, on white: a two-line deck at about 1.4vw on a 1% left margin, and from 42% across a two-line title at 8.3vw, medium weight, tracking -0.06em. Bottom row: mono credit left, scroll cue and arrow aligned to the title column.
references.type: Beausite Classic, a grotesk with some stroke contrast, in Medium for titles and Regular for text; sentence case, tracking -0.06em at display size. Geist Mono for small uppercase labels. Steps: 8.3vw title, about 5.5vw numerals, about 3vw statements, 16px body, 10px mono. Footer wordmark near 96vw.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #fe7141 #cdabfe #d1ddd3 #f0ff1c — White base with flat blocks of orange, lilac, sage and black assigned to whole modules (stat tiles, quote panels, chapter bands), all drawn from the hero footage. Text is black, or off-white on black.
references.imagery: Hero: abstract blurred video with a heat-map grade, cut into overlapping rectangles. Body: warm documentary photos and clips of people at desks in wood-lined rooms, square-cornered, butted directly against flat colour blocks with no gap.
references.layout: 1% margins and a recurring column line at about 42% where most headings and text begin. Open white text passages ruled by hairlines alternate with tight mosaics in which photos and colour blocks share edges. Each chapter opens with a full-width colour band.

sections.description: A full-width hairline, a tiny mono label at the left, then seven black partner logos evenly spaced across the full width in one row with generous padding above and below, closed by a second hairline. Immediately beneath, another mono label and a three-line statement at about 3vw, flush left and occupying only the left half, followed by a full-width photo strip.

A mosaic with no gutters. A photo of two people at a laptop fills the left two-thirds at roughly 1:1; the right third is split into two stacked flat tiles, lilac above and sage below. Each tile carries a large numeral with a plus sign at about 5.5vw in its top-left corner and a two-line caption directly beneath; the rest of the tile is empty colour.

Quote module as two abutting blocks: a black block on the left 40% holding only a small name and a mono role caption, and a sage block on the right 60% with the quotation at about 3vw, top-left aligned with empty sage beneath. Directly below, a full-width orange band opens a chapter: hairline at top, a large two-digit number with the chapter word under it at left, a two-line title and small paragraph starting at the 42% column.

Black footer. A row of three small source counts along the top, separated by vertical hairlines, then the report name in off-white heavy type at nearly full viewport width with a trademark sign at its top-right, then the year at the same size right-aligned on a second line. Two small link columns with mono headings sit lower left beside the year; a hairline and one row of credits and partner logos close it.

steal: Start most headings and text at a fixed column line about 42% across, leaving the left for small decks, credits and chapter numbers.
Butt flat colour tiles directly against a photograph with no gutter and put one large numeral plus two caption lines in each tile's top-left corner.
Take the page's flat block colours from the hero footage so the abstract video and the layout read as one palette.
references.media: A video collage covers 100% of the screen at load and lifts to the top ~53% to uncover the title on white. Below, a documentary photograph two thirds wide in a sticky frame beside stacked colour stat blocks, a pinned deck of colour cards each with a 10s clip docked bottom-left, and a carousel of equal stills running off the right edge: 12 images and 6 muted videos, all square-cornered.
references.motion: No preloader, but the collage re-cuts itself for about 4s before the title lands. Framer drives the sticky stacking (a 1350px photo frame and three 900px chapter cards that peel away to uncover the next); there is no split text, links change colour over .2s cubic-bezier(.44,0,.56,1), and one panel slides 610px in over 500ms cubic-bezier(0.44,0,0.37,1).

references.name: USAvionix
references.idea: A maker of autonomous jet drones explains its product as a single mission played out on scroll: one pinned WebGL camera flies from a lone drone over forested mountains to a swarm, to detection overlays and then to a dark tactical map, while a console readout runs at the edges and three status colours (observed, threat, secured) carry the plot.
references.hero: After a preloader that shows only the dimmed drone silhouette for over 4.5s, a full-bleed real-time scene: photoreal forested mountains seen from above with a matte black flying wing dead centre, wingspan about 560px (39% of the width). A three-line claim at 80px (5.6vw), Geist 600, -0.04em, leading 0.95, sits top-left at x=32, y 88-300; a three-line 29px lead is docked bottom-right (x 874-1384) over a translucent grey pill about 248x40 that prompts the scroll. A grey contact pill and a menu button are fixed top-right, and a one-word chapter code with sliding tick rails sits top-centre. The middle 60% belongs to the scene.
references.type: Two faces from one superfamily. Geist (41% of characters) at 600 for heads: 80px in the hero (5.6vw, leading 0.95, -0.04em), 76px chapter titles, 50px post-story heads; 29px leads at 500 and 17-19px body. Geist Mono (59%) at 11-12px uppercase, +0.06em, for the telemetry. Sentence case except the mono. The house version keeps Geist alone and sets the readout in sentence case at 16px with tabular figures.
references.colour: #000000 #0f0f0f #ffffff #7aebff #ff6666 #ffcb47 — A black page and near-black scene ground with white text, and three status accents with one job each: amber for observed and the detection boxes, coral for threat, cyan for secured, each under 5% of the text and never on chrome. The terrain brings olive and slate; the closing cards bring warm orange.
references.imagery: Real-time photoreal terrain in a cool, desaturated olive and slate grade with volumetric haze; a matte black flying-wing drone; flat 1px overlay props (bounding boxes with confidence labels, ID tags joined by dotted lines, a sensor cone, curved flight trails, ripple rings); a satellite-style photograph of a village; then warm sunset and dusk renders of a wildfire, a desert ridge and a substation as the payoff.
references.layout: One full-bleed sticky canvas carries 14 chapters over about 60,000px of runway (about 4500px each), with text docked in the corners at 32px margins: title top-left, lead bottom-left or bottom-right at most about 500px wide, telemetry bottom-right, chapter code top-centre. After the story the page returns to normal flow on black for an expanding three-card row and a split with a wireframe globe; margins drift from 32 to 40 to 48px. 72 screens for 435 words.

sections.description: The camera pulls back to three drones in a loose triangle, each with a small white ID tag, the tags joined by dotted lines; a 76px two-line title top-left and, bottom-right from x=732, a 29px lead over a four-row spec table with a label column and lighter values.

Detection: back over the terrain, about 25 small yellow bounding boxes (40-60px) with label chips naming an object class and a confidence percentage, the drone small at the centre, and a four-line readout bottom-right with coordinates, altitude, speed and counts.

A tactical map: a #0f0f0f ground with a faint perspective grid, an irregular outline of a land area covering about 40% of the width, a tag on its edge and three hotspots with 6s ripple rings. Over three chapters the hotspots and tag change colour (amber for survey, coral for threat, cyan for services on site) as grey drone glyphs fly in on curved trails.

After the dark story, three photographic renders in a row from x=48 to 1392 with 24px gaps: one open card 660px wide and two closed at 318px, all about 628px tall with about 10px corners, the open one carrying a 29px title and a three-line 15px description bottom-left.

steal: Tell a product's capability as one pinned scene: about 4500px of scroll per chapter, the camera moving continuously and the text still, changing only by opacity (out over 250ms, in over 400ms after a 200ms delay).

Give colour a job: three status accents, each tied to one state of the story and used only on tags, hotspots and single status words, never on chrome, each under 5% of the text, on black with white type.

After a cold, dark story, pay off with warm photographs in normal flow: an expanding row of three, one open at about 660px and two closed at about 318px. The site speaks in monospace telemetry over hairline grids; the house version sets the readout in the text face with tabular figures and lets the scene carry the structure.
references.media: One sticky full-bleed WebGL scene covers 100% of every story screen, with an SVG overlay drawing the boxes, tags, trails and ripple rings over it; after the story come three photographic mission cards and a wireframe globe bleeding off the right and bottom edges. Two canvases, four images, no video.
references.motion: A preloader of 4.5s or more shows only the dimmed model, then Lenis drives one pinned canvas through about 60,000px: the drone turns from banked to top-down, the camera pulls back to the formation, rises into the mesh, dives to a sensor view and cuts to the map, where zone colours change by chapter. Text moves by opacity only through 346 WAAPI fades (250ms ease-out, 400ms ease-in-out after 200ms), HUD marks transform over 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), 64 ripple rings loop on 6s, and there is no reduced-motion rule.
